profile.summary: Sei is a deep learning model that reads a 4-kb human DNA sequence and predicts the probability of 21,907 chromatin profiles (transcription factor binding, histone marks and chromatin accessibility) at its centre. Those predictions are then summarised into 40 sequence classes, such as promoter, cell type-specific enhancer or Polycomb-repressed, which give a score for a sequence or for the effect of a variant.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Results (model) and Methods; README: introduction

summary_quotes.text: which takes as input a 4-kilobase (kb) length sequence and predicts the probabilities of 21,907

Sei provides a global map from any sequence to regulatory activities, as represented by 40 sequence classes, and each sequence class integrates predictions for 21,907 chromatin profiles (transcription factor, histone marks, and chromatin accessibility profiles across a wide range of cell types).
Sequence classes provide a global classification and quantification of sequence and variant effects based on diverse regulatory activities, such as cell type-specific enhancer functions.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The Sei model has three parts: a convolutional network with parallel linear and nonlinear paths, residual dilated convolution layers that widen the receptive field without losing resolution, and a B-spline basis layer that reduces 256 spatial bins to 16 before fully connected output layers. It was trained with Selene in PyTorch as a multi-label classifier: for each 4-kb region, the label is whether the centre base overlaps a peak in each of the 21,907 profiles. The authors then predicted 30 million genome positions at a 100-bp step, reduced the predictions with PCA and clustered them with Louvain community detection. The 40 largest clusters are the sequence classes. A sequence's class score is a projection of its chromatin predictions onto each class vector; for variants the score is alt minus ref, with histone predictions adjusted for nucleosome occupancy.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Methods, Model architecture and training, Sequence classes; README: Sequence class prediction

quotes.text: The model architecture is composed of three sequential sections: (1) a convolutional network with dual linear and nonlinear paths; (2) residual dilated convolution layers; (3) spatial basis function transformation and output layers.
Dilated convolutional layers with residual connections further expand the receptive fields without reducing spatial resolution.

a B-spline basis matrix (256 × 16) with 16 degrees of freedom across 256 uniformly spaced spatial bins is generated and multiplied with the convolutional layers output to reduce the 256 spatial dimensions to 16 spline basis function dimensions
a 21,907 dimensional binary label vector was created for the 21,907
The model was implemented in PyTorch and trained with Selene.
We selected 30 million genomic positions that uniformly tile the genome with a 100-bp step size
We refer to the largest 40 clusters as sequence classes
Raw sequence class scores are projection scores of chromatin profile predictions projected on the unit-length vectors representing each sequence class.
Computed as alt - ref of the raw sequence class scores **adjusted for nucleosome occupancy, i.e. histone normalized**.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There is one released Sei model, published on Zenodo (record 4906996, dated 2021-06-07) as a 3,281,639,255-byte archive. The repository download script fetches it, with a resources archive holding hg19 and hg38 FASTA files. Whole-genome sequence class annotations for hg38, and for hg19 lifted over from hg38, are in a separate Zenodo record, and the authors recommend these annotations over raw sequence class scores for reference genome sequences. The training configuration is in train/train.yml. A result should name the repository commit and the Zenodo model record; this page read commit 1e16bff9.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Supervised deep learning sequence model that predicts chromatin profiles from DNA, with a sequence class layer built on its predictions.

quotes.text: Sei learns a vocabulary of regulatory activities, called sequence classes, using a deep learning model that predicts 21,907 chromatin profiles

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Convolutional network with dual linear and nonlinear paths, residual dilated convolutions, a B-spline spatial basis layer (256 bins to 16), then a fully connected layer and an output layer.

quotes.text: (1) a convolutional network with dual linear and nonlinear paths; (2) residual dilated convolution layers; (3) spatial basis function transformation and output layers
a fully connected layer and an output layer are used to integrate information across the whole sequence and generate the final 21,907 dimensional predictions

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A 4,096-base DNA sequence. The scripts accept a BED or FASTA file for sequences, or a VCF file for variants (hg19 or hg38).

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Probabilities for 21,907 chromatin profiles at the sequence centre, written as HDF5 files; 40 sequence class scores; for variants, ref and alt predictions and sequence class variant effect scores as TSV and NPY files.

strengths.text: Covers a wide set of regulatory signals in one model: 21,907 profiles spanning about 1,000 DNA-binding proteins, 77 histone marks and chromatin accessibility in more than 1,300 cell lines and tissues.

quotes.text: The Sei model encompasses an estimated 1,000 nonhistone DNA-binding proteins (which we refer to as TFs), 77 histone marks and chromatin accessibility across

strengths.text: The 40 sequence classes give a compact, interpretable summary of a sequence or variant effect, grouped as promoter, enhancer, CTCF, TF binding, Polycomb, heterochromatin, transcription and low signal.

quotes.text: we grouped sequence classes into groups including P (Promoter), E (Enhancer), CTCF (CTCF-cohesin binding), TF (TF binding), PC (Polycomb-repressed), HET (Heterochromatin), TN (Transcription), and L (Low Signal) sequence classes

strengths.text: The authors report an average AUROC of 0.972 and AUPRC of 0.409 across all 21,907 profiles on held-out chromosomes, and a 19% average improvement over their earlier DeepSEA Beluga model on the 2,002 shared profiles.

run_guide.summary: Get the Sei code, download the trained model and reference files, and score the bundled test VCF for chromatin profile and sequence class variant effects.
prerequisites: A new Anaconda environment with Python 3.6+, PyTorch (>=1.0), Selene (>=0.5.0) and docopt, as the README asks. PyTorch and Selene are installed by following their own instructions.
A CUDA GPU for chromatin profile prediction, as the README advises; the sequence class step runs on CPU.
About 3.3 GB of disk for the model archive, plus the resources archive.
Code is for academic and research use only; weights are CC BY 4.0 on Zenodo.
